definitions.explanation: A fixed expression consisting of four kanji characters, often derived from classical Chinese. These are a distinctive feature of the Japanese language and are commonly tested in school examinations.

examples.japanese: {四字熟語|よじじゅくご}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦テスト→テスト：01065_tesuto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There's a test on four-character idioms.

examples.japanese: ⟦{一石二鳥|いっせきにちょう}→一石二鳥：04764_issekinichou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{使|つか}われる→使う：00473_tsukau⟧{四字熟語|よじじゅくご}だ。
examples.english: "Killing two birds with one stone" is a commonly used four-character idiom.

examples.japanese: ⟦スピーチ→スピーチ：03852_supiichi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{四字熟語|よじじゅくご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{格調|かくちょう}⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦{印象|いんしょう}→印象：01846_inshou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{与|あた}える→与える：01821_ataeru⟧。
examples.english: Including four-character idioms in a speech gives an impression of refinement.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Four-character compounds are an important part of Japanese education and literacy. Students learn them throughout elementary and middle school, and they frequently appear on exams. Many are borrowed from classical Chinese texts. Examples include ⟦{一期一会|いちごいちえ}→一期一会：04768_ichigoichie⟧ (once-in-a-lifetime encounter), ⟦{以心伝心|いしんでんしん}→以心伝心：04766_ishindenshin⟧ (unspoken understanding), and ⟦{弱肉強食|じゃくにくきょうしょく}→弱肉強食：05946_jakunikukyoushoku⟧ (survival of the fittest).

FORMS:
{四|よ}⟦{字|じ}→字：01606_ji⟧ (four characters) + ⟦{熟語|じゅくご}→熟語：04219_jukugo⟧ (compound word).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{熟語|じゅくご}→熟語：04219_jukugo⟧: compound word (any length)
- ⟦{慣用句|かんようく}→慣用句：15890_kanyouku⟧: idiomatic expression (not limited to four characters)
- ⟦{故事成語|こじせいご}→故事成語：18562_kojiseigo⟧: proverb derived from classical stories
